thread:
aj: Quick one — customers are hitting 429 cascades when clients do high-concurrency pagination + generation. We should ship a tiny demo that shows 'rate smoothing' + backpressure across pages so integrators can copy. Anyone got a preferred pattern?

maria: 429 cascades sounds like clients opening too many inflight requests rather than respecting quotas. We should show a token-bucket + per-endpoint concurrency semaphore imo.

kevin: Agree. Also need to handle missing Retry-After headers: sometimes we only get x-ratelimit-reset or nothing. Demo should include a safe fallback (exponential backoff + jitter) and show respecting Retry-After when present.

aj: Example log we saw: `2026-02-15T22:11:02Z GET /v1/generate 429 headers:{'x-request-id': 'abc', 'x-rate-limit-reset': '167658'}` — client kept retrying immediately and blew up.

olivia: +1. For JS sample we can use `p-limit` for concurrency + a tiny token bucket. Something like:
```js
// pseudo
const limit = pLimit(8); // max concurrent
const bucket = new TokenBucket({capacity: 20, refillPerSec: 5});
await Promise.all(pages.map(page => limit(() => {
  return bucket.take(1).then(() => api.fetchPage(page));
})));
```
This smooths bursts and keeps the number of inflight requests bounded.

luca: For Python async, `aiolimiter` + `asyncio.Semaphore` works well. Also show an example of parsing headers safely: `retry_after = int(headers.get('Retry-After') or headers.get('x-rate-limit-reset', 0))`.

maria: We should also show a pagination pattern that yields results progressively rather than firing off all page requests at once. Example pattern in pseudocode: `for await page in paginated(api): await queue.put(page);` with limited workers consuming the queue.

kevin: There's an SDK parity bug: JS SDK auto-batching counts requests differently than Python when you call `client.generate` concurrently — JS increments the 'inflight' counter on call start, Python increments on send. This discrepancy affects client-side backpressure examples. We should note that in demo and open a ticket.

aj: Good catch. Can someone open a bug for SDK parity and link it in the demo README? Tag it `sdk/parity-rate-counting`.

olivia: I'll draft the JS demo and README. Plan: repo `redwood-examples/rate-smoothing-demo` with short README, diagrams, and two runnable scripts `run_demo_js.js` and `run_demo_py.py`. README will include configurable knobs: concurrency, bucket size, refill rate, page size.

kevin: I'll do the Python port and a small harness that simulates quota headers so folks can play locally (include a `--simulate-429` flag).

luca: Small test cases to include: 1) burst of 100 concurrent page requests; 2) steady stream at threshold; 3) missing Retry-After header behavior.

aj: Action items: olivia -> JS demo PR draft by EOD Friday; kevin -> Py port by next Tue; aj -> open SDK parity ticket and add integration test suggestions. I'll add the ticket: https://redwood-internal/issue/RI-2147 (placeholder).

deploy-bot: Deployed branch `rate-smoothing-demo` to staging for manual test. :rocket:

maria: Nice. One more thing — add a short section in README about on-boarding: "If you see repeated 429s, reduce client concurrency or enable token-bucket mode." Keep wording prescriptive.

aj: Perfect. If anyone has snippets they'd like included ping me here. Closing thread for now, will update when PRs land.
